question: Drains exiting from Mohenjo-Daro had ______ doors that were probably closed at night to prevent vagrants or negative elements from entering the city through that access.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Wooden**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The drains of Mohenjo-Daro were equipped with **wooden doors**, which were likely used to secure the city at night.
 
• Mohenjo-Daro, part of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization, had an advanced drainage system demonstrating urban planning expertise.
 
• The wooden doors on drains were designed to prevent access by vagrants or harmful elements, ensuring the city's safety and hygiene.
 
• Wood was a commonly used material in the Indus Valley Civilization for construction purposes, including doors and other structures.
 
• This feature reflects the civilization's emphasis on maintaining order and security within their urban settlements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohenjo-Daro:** It is one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley Civilization, located in present-day Pakistan.
 
• **Drainage System:** The Indus Valley cities had a sophisticated drainage system, with covered drains made of bricks running along the streets.
 
• **Urban Planning:** Mohenjo-Daro was laid out in a grid pattern, indicating advanced town planning methods for its time.
 
• **Material Use:** Wood, along with mud bricks and baked bricks, was extensively used in construction within the civilization.
 
• **Security Measures:** The presence of wooden doors on drains highlights the civilization's awareness of safety and urban management challenges.
